expectations.text: Converts inline style strings to React object syntax (e.g., maxWidth: '60ch')
expectations.evidence: The output converts style="max-width: 60ch; margin: auto" to style={{ maxWidth: '60ch', margin: 'auto' }} and style="margin-top: 1rem" to style={{ marginTop: '1rem' }}. Both use camelCase keys and string values in object syntax.

expectations.text: Uses className='wa-grid' on the div (not class)
expectations.evidence: The div element uses className="wa-grid" (line 10-11 of the code block), correctly converting from HTML class to React className.

expectations.text: Handles CSS custom property --min-column-size in style object
expectations.evidence: The output uses style={{ '--min-column-size': '200px' } as React.CSSProperties} on the div. The custom property is kept as a quoted string key, and the as React.CSSProperties type assertion is applied to satisfy TypeScript, which is the correct pattern.

expectations.text: Maps wa-textarea to Textarea, wa-switch to Switch
expectations.evidence: Import statement: import { Input, Switch, Textarea } from '@/components/ui'. Usage: <Textarea label="Bio" rows={4} .../> and <Switch checked>Enable notifications</Switch>. Both wa-textarea and wa-switch are correctly mapped to PascalCase wrapper components.

expectations.text: Preserves boolean attributes (required, checked) as props
expectations.evidence: The Input components use bare 'required' prop: <Input label="First name" required />. The Switch uses bare 'checked' prop: <Switch checked>. Both are JSX boolean shorthand, correctly preserved.

expectations.text: Does NOT fabricate onSwitchChange or similar events
expectations.evidence: No event handler props appear anywhere in the output. The Switch component has only 'checked' as a prop with children text. No onSwitchChange, onChange, onWaChange, or any fabricated event handlers are present.

claims.claim: All required components are already installed in your project (Input, Textarea, Switch)
claims.evidence: This claim cannot be verified from the output alone -- it depends on the project state. However, it is reasonable guidance text, not a code correctness issue.

claims.claim: rows="4" converted to rows={4} as JSX number expression
claims.evidence: The code shows rows={4} on the Textarea component, correctly converting the string attribute to a numeric JSX expression.

claims.claim: Self-closing tags used for Input and Textarea
claims.evidence: <Input label="First name" required /> and <Textarea label="Bio" rows={4} style={{ marginTop: '1rem' }} /> both use self-closing syntax.

claims.claim: Single import from @/components/ui using the configured alias
claims.evidence: The import statement reads: import { Input, Switch, Textarea } from '@/components/ui' -- a single consolidated import.

suggestions.reason: No assertion verifies that rows="4" is converted to the numeric expression rows={4} rather than the string rows="4". This is an important JSX conversion detail that the skill handled correctly but could regress without detection.

suggestions.assertion: Handles CSS custom property --min-column-size in style object
suggestions.reason: This assertion could be strengthened by also checking for the 'as React.CSSProperties' type assertion, which is necessary for TypeScript to accept custom properties in style objects. Without it, the code would produce a type error.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertions cover the key inline-style and JSX conversion concerns well. The absence-check for fabricated events is a good discriminating assertion. Minor gap: no check for numeric attribute conversion (rows).
